sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: This part adds up most of the inputs with fixed weights: through it, each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 28% at 0 to about 90% at 2 vessels for a typical patient, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; chest pain brought on by exercise takes it to about 78%, a flat rather than upsloping ST segment to about 69% and a thallium scan other than normal to about 56%.

Higher cholesterol (from about 17% at 193 mg/dL to about 47% at 308 mg/dL) and older age (from about 22% at 42 to about 32% at 66 years) raise it steadily, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG raise it to about 33%.

sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: Being a woman lowers it to about 1%, typical angina and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL each to about 5% and non-anginal chest pain to about 7%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 39% at 118 to about 22% at 175 beats per minute; atypical angina instead raises it through this part, to about 39%.

parts.original_hypothesis: Composition (parallel children feeding one ReLU): 2065 = relu(-0.618 + 0.847 sex:1 - 1.26 fbs:1 + 0.483 exang:1 - 0.473 slope:3 + 0.51 thal:6 + 0.136 thal:7 + 0.625 angina_bp_chain - 0.299 bp_hr_ramp), read out -1.63 into the logit. Hypothesis: a sub-additivity correction for the linear score's male and angina terms. It opens for men (60% open vs 7% of women), angina patients (71% vs 28%), cp:2 men (88%), thal:6/thal:7; fasting sugar fbs:1 closes it completely (0 of 33 open); higher resting BP/HR (via both children) narrows it. When open it subtracts 1.63*2065 (mean 2.3 logit among the 42% open). Evidence (train, 242 rows, counterfactual flips through the full model): male-vs-female effect +3.06 logit without angina but +1.36 with angina (linear part alone +3.25); angina effect +1.61 for women but +0.06 for men (linear part +2.23); cp:2 effect -1.48 in men vs -0.27 in women; d logit/d trestbps +0.81 per SD in gate-open patients vs +0.10 in closed. So: male sex and exercise angina are each strong risk signals but do not add up, and among such patients cp:2 chest pain and low BP mark lower risk. Mean-ablating the gate drops train AUC 0.954 -> 0.920 and raises log-loss 0.281 -> 0.379; within the open subgroup AUC 0.949 vs 0.903 without the gate. Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a clearly higher predicted risk of heart disease if exercise brings on chest pain (about 78%) than if exercise does not bring on chest pain (about 28%).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 69%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 28%) (on the training data only).

Through this part, the model treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 17% at 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to about 47% at 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) (on the training data only).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment) lowers it (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 17 training patients (a downsloping ST segment).
